own_solution.law: The de Broglie relation is lambda = h/p. Non-relativistically, K = p²/(2m), so lambda = hc/sqrt(2(mc²)K). With K = 150 eV and mc² = 511000 eV, lambda = 1240/sqrt(2 × 511000 × 150) nm.
assumptions: The electron is treated non-relativistically, as instructed.
The stated kinetic energy is its kinetic energy when the wavelength is determined.
The separate particles in the disconnected sentences do not interact with the electron.

notes: Both relevant sentences raise the electron's kinetic energy to 250 eV, giving lambda = 1240/sqrt(2 × 511000 × 250) = 0.077576 nm. The other sentences attach the added energy to separate particles with no stated physical path to the target electron. All four variants consistently specify a further 100 eV of kinetic energy; their attachment and delivery wording vary. The remote-particle additions are somewhat contrived but introduce no physics defect. Numerical results retain calculation digits; approximately 0.100 nm and 0.0776 nm are suitable rounded answers.
